name: @vibe-agent-toolkit/cli

scripts.build: tsx src/utils/validate-help-files.ts && tsx ../dev-tools/src/tsc-clean-build.ts && bun run generate:schemas && tsx ../dev-tools/src/prepare-bin.ts

author: Jeff Dutton
//dependencies-note: DO NOT add example agent packages or adopter packages here. Adopter packages (like vat-development-agents) depend on the CLI binary at build time — declaring them as deps creates a circular build dependency. They are built in a second turbo pass via package#task overrides in turbo.json.
//peerDependencies-note: The RAG backends are OPTIONAL PEERS, never optionalDependencies. `optionalDependencies` are INSTALLED BY DEFAULT by npm and pnpm alike - 'optional' there means the install may fail without failing the build, not that it is skipped - so declaring them that way shipped ~287 MB unpacked (onnxruntime-web 137.5 MB, a LanceDB platform binary 97.8 MB, gpt-tokenizer 42.2 MB, apache-arrow 5.3 MB, protobufjs 3.0 MB; measured on darwin-arm64 against this release's pins, and the platform binary is larger on win32-x64) to every adopter, contradicting the seam in src/utils/optional-backend.ts that exists precisely to keep them out. Optional peers are NOT auto-installed, so the manifest now says what that module already says: these ship separately, and an absent one is a legible error naming the package to install. projection-sqlite is deliberately NOT in this group: it has zero third-party dependencies (only node:sqlite, which is built into Node) and a 152 KB dist, so the platform-binary argument that justifies the seam is simply false for it. It is also what `vat resources query` builds its ephemeral in-memory store from, and a query surface that works only where a backend was separately installed is the capability gate the projection design forbids.
